recipes.name: Tourtière (French Canadian Meat Pie)
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.1 ounce) package double-crust pie pastry, thawed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
Prick potato several times with a fork and place onto a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until easily pierced with a fork, 50 minutes to 1 hour. Let cool for 10 minutes, then discard skin and mash flesh. Turn the oven off.
Place mashed potato into a large skillet with ground pork, onion, water, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and allpsice. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until very thick, at least 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Line a deep-dish pie plate with one pastry. Spoon in pork and potato filling.
Cover with remaining pastry. Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with paprika. Cut a steam vent in pastry.
Bake in the preheated oven for 50 minutes. If the edges brown too fast, cover them with a strip of foil. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Tourtière (French Canadian Meat Pie)
raw_recipe.description: A tourtière is a French Canadian meat pie made with deliciously seasoned ground pork, mashed potatoes, and onion in a double crust pie pastry.

review.reviewBody:
I am french canadian and meat pie has been a family tradition for years, made by my Memere's, but is a long lost art as we have americanized our traditions. I made it this thanksgiving with the help of my Aunt and she says leave out the cinnamon but use more allspice in it's place, do not add water, and add the potato after you cook the meat, little by little until you feel it is perfect for you. I did 2 pies, one this one way and one her way, and she was right. But both were very tasty and did not last the night. Will definetly be making again for Christmas Eve. Thanks!

UPDATE: TO THE REVIEW WHO'S PIE HAD CHUNKS OF POTATO, SAVE ONE POTATO FOR DICIING BUT USE THE REMAINING POTATOES FOR MASHING INTO THE MEAT. THE POTATOS IS THE TRICK FOR KEEPING THE MEAT FROM BEING CRUMBLY..UPDATE #2, USE HALF PORK, HALF GROUND BEEF. YUMMY!

This is super good. I used around two pounds pork, a little over a pound of ground beef (Did not drain). Added 4 cloves garlic. Cooked onion, garlic and meat together with 1-1/2 tsp salt and 1 tsp pepper. Then added 1/2 tsp allspice, 1/4 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp cloves, 1/2 tsp smoked paprika into filling. 2 mashed baked potatoes, and no water! Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. Baked one pie in a 10 inch cast Iron skillet and also made a second 8 inch pie. Would make two 9 inch pies beautifully. You must do an egg wash and sprinkle with paprika. Gives it such beautiful color. Love this. Going to reheat it for breakfast and top with a runny egg. Oh man, Super excited.

Wonderful! Every year or so I make foods from a different country for Christmas. This year I chose France. I never expected a spiced MEAT pie to be something I would love. It made me think of minced meat. But, it came up in my search for French foods and my husband and I thought we’d give it a go and did a preliminary test drive. Definitely will repeat this one and make double for when the kids come! Thank you Lynmarie for your suggestions! We ground a pork loin for the meat, cooked the potato in the microwave, left out the cinnamon and used 1/4 teaspoon allspice. However, we did add the water because the meat was so lean there was almost no fat. We kept adding water all along to help the cooking process, but, I’m not sure I’d suggest doing that next time. I think I’d just turn down the heat some. However, it cooked down pretty quickly and we took a potato masher to the mixture as it cooked to help it mix together better. We cooked it on medium in an iron skillet and it took less than 40 minutes for it to thicken and be ready to place in the pie crust and bake.. I’m glad we didn’t include the cinnamon and didn’t add garlic as someone suggested. I think both would over power the subtleties of the dish. Very good and worth the time.

It’s been a while since I made this and I forgot how tasty it is! I cooked the potato in my instant pot (about 20 mins depending on the size of the potato) and mashed it. When I waited for the pressure to release I started browning the meats (I used 1/2 ground pork, 1/2 ground beef). Added all the spices (doubling allspice, halved cinnamon; added garlic powder) and water and let it simmer. Then I added the mashed potato and let that thicken, on low, for about 20 minutes. Then I added everything in the pie crust, sealed with top crust, and sprinkled on smoked paprika (didn’t use the egg). The finished product was awesome!

This is the type of recipe I like to make, minimal ingredients, maximum flavor. Like others, I used the Pillsbury prepared pie crusts and combined about 75% ground pork and 25% ground chuck. I also used 1/4 cup red wine in addition to 1/2 cup water, and added one minced carrot for a bit of sweetness. I sautéed the onion and carrots for about 3 minutes in olive oil, then added the meat mixture for a few minutes, then added the rest of the ingredients while the meat was still pink. In all other aspects, I prepared exactly as the recipe was written, and the mixture was ready in about 45 minutes to fill the pie shell. The pie came out great, and made four generous servings. I will make this again.

I used 2 large pork chops baked to render the fat, Used old-fashioned crank-operated meat grinder to grind the meat, baked potato and raw onion. Did not cook anything in water but mixed ingredients together and baked in two-crust pie. It turned out exactly like Pork Pies made by Canadian French cooks I have known.

LOVE the flavors of this recipe!!!! I bake the potato in the microwave to save time, sometimes I use two potatoes to make it more filling. While the potato is baking in the microwave, I add all other items to the pan except the water and get that all cooked up. I add the potato and water when the meat is done cooking, and just cook for a couple minutes to get all incorporated, then add to the pie. Very similar to current directions, but it cuts about 45 minutes off the stove time, which is nice! I’ve made this multiple times this year, and look forward to making it for the holidays!

Just yesterday I made 4 meat pies. Today this recipe shows up on Pinterest! I'm having company for supper tonight and am serving meat pie with a salad, cranberries, jello and strawberry shortcake. These people have never had it, so should be fun to see what they think. I am French Canadian and the recipe I use I got from making these pies with my grandmother many years ago.Similar but we use 1/2 beef and 1/2 pork. I cook the meat, drain it good and then add the chopped onion, then water, spices are different. We use a heavy dose of sage, a little garlic, salt, fresh ground black pepper and some minced onion bits. I simmer all of this, then start adding the instant potatoes to thicken to the right consistency.
I also sneak in a few dashes of cayenne pepper for my Scott Irish husband. Just to give it a slight kick. I am wondering why we use sage and others are using cinnamon and allspice. There is supposed to be a spice jar sold in Canada that has a mixture of these spices for the pie. Does anyone know what this is called? I also whip up an egg and 'frost' my pies with that and they are a very nice brown when they come out of the oven. I will try some cinnamon and allspice next time instead of sage, just for fun.

This was very good! More trouble than I'd take on a weeknight, but fine for a weekend. We used mashed potato flakes instead of baking a potato, and browned the pork and onions before simmering them in chicken stock. We also used store-bought pie crusts. I used a bit more allspice than the recipe said and added some garlic powder, but otherwise kept the spices the same as the recipe. It smelled delicious in the oven, and tasted great. We'll definitely make this again some time.

Delicious. I use puff pastry I also saved half of the meat and used puff pastry to make sausage rolls they were to die for. Just roll out the puff pastry I rolled the puff pastry out a little enough to make 6 sausage rolls. Place a small meat (sausage size) on each piece of pastry and roll them up, coat with egg wash and bake at 400f for 20-25 min.

This was quite good. I did make a few changes: half ground pork/half ground beef. Used sage and fresh garlic in addition to the other spices. I also found this needed extra salt and pepper. I layered my pie: first half-baked sliced sweet potatoes, meat mixture, peeled and sliced pears, and more meat mixture. 

DO microwave your potato instead of baking it. 15 mins on high and you're done. Life saver.
Add a side salad and it's perfect.

I’ve made tourtiere pies for 50 years. I add a chopped onion to 5 pounds of ground pork and all the spices and water mentioned into a kettle. I start it to boiling then turn it down and let it cook for at least two hours making sure the pork is all cooked down and so are the onions.. they usually will be a lot of juice so I make sure to drain some of it because I don’t want my pie crust to be wet and soggy. Once drained to my liking, I add two medium size cooked and mashed potato to the pork mixture. This makes enough for two pies. I bake one and the other one I wrap tightly in saran and then tinfoil over that and put it in the freezer uncooked. In order to bake that one when I’m ready I unwrap it. Make sure my oven is preheated to 375 put the frozen pie in the oven and cook between 65 and 70 minutes.
I made this. The only thing I changed was I had to use gold potatoes and I used a premade crust. My husband and I loved it!

Thank you for such an informative forum! I'm a first timer here, and having never been to Canada, haden't heard of this pastry before now. However, I will be making it next week for a gathering that we're hosting. and having read many of the comments, I will tweek it a bit by omitting the cinnamon and using pork and beef. Can't wait to try it! Oh, and one note to Cheryn's comment regarding grounding a LEAN pork loin instead of using pork sausage, perhaps add some bacon fat, lard, or shortening while cooking it, rather than just water? It may not be the healthiest option if you're making this every week, but for a splurge on a special occasion, it will make a world of difference and provide satiety with every bite. Or, perhaps instead of grinding and boiling, you could roast the loin using a slow, moist method, then, instead of grinding it, shread it and add it, along with the drippings to the other ingredients on the stove?
Simple and tasty

I was so happy to see this recipe in your files. I have a Canadian friend who shared this recipe with me years ago and it has been a family favorite of ours. I will admit that I have never used the allspice with it but will definitely try it next time. Another favorite to add to this recipe is just a small handful of raisins. You can also use a mixture of pork and beef or just beef. The great thing about this recipe is you can adjust it to your family's liking but definitely try the straight recipe first you may find you love it.

This Tourtiere recipe is the best one I've ever used. I make it for Christmas eve, this is a Canadian tradition. I usually make 2 or 3 and we deliver a couple to our friends from Quebec as part of a gift.
perfect spice amounts

Found this recipe years ago looking for an appropriate dish to celebrate NHL playoffs, and it has been our Christmas morning breakfast ever since! Not only is it delicious, it makes the whole house smell heavenly. Super easy and a crowd pleaser? Yes, please!
